Thanks Rishi / Daniel — pulled together a preliminary packaging suggestion below (high-level):

Proposed SKU decomposition for private offer (recommended):
- SKU-A: Reserved capacity (12-month commit) — primary discountable SKU
- SKU-B: Burst on-demand credits (metered) — lower discount, separate line
- SKU-C: Support & onboarding (fixed one-time)
- SKU-FIN: Financing fee (separate line item, labeled Financing — passthrough-friendly)

Pass-through mechanics (for CloudProcure):
- Apply Redwood private-offer discounts at the SKU level, produce net invoice.
- Evergreen requests pass-through % on net invoice line: we recommend 5% pass-through to CloudProcure on net (applies to SKU-A and SKU-B after discounts).
- If Evergreen prefers pass-through on gross list, note this increases net cost to Redwood; need approval from Finance.

Margin uplift / incentives:
- If commit velocity hits 120% of Q1 forecast, increase reseller uplift to 8% for Q2 (to motivate forward selling).

Notes on financing:
- Recommend SKU-FIN be a separate, non-discountable line (so financing provider sees the full financed amount). We can map SKU-FIN to a different GL code for your treasury.
- If Evergreen wants amortization on the same invoice, we can produce amortized installments but the payoff/servicing will require a finance supplier on the PO.

I'll draft a one-page layout and include numbers. Jordan

Quick ops note re: separate financing SKU and invoice routing to CloudProcure:

1) Separate financing SKU: Operationally straightforward. We will configure SKU-FIN as a non-discountable line, map to GL 'Financing', and ensure it appears as a distinct line on the PDF invoice. No changes needed to our billing engine for that format.

2) Invoice routing: If you want the invoice to be sent to CloudProcure for collection while Evergreen receives a copy, we need a reseller billing mandate or reseller agreement uploaded to our portal (legal/finance requirement). We can also route only the payment instructions to CloudProcure and still bill Evergreen.

3) Evidence for procurement: procurement will want a short certificate showing reseller margin applied to each invoice for audit. We can generate a monthly CSV export that shows SKU-level list, discounts, net, and reseller pass-through % as supporting evidence.

4) Timeline for PO processing: once we have the PO and reseller mandate, ops can lock the private offer in 2 business days.

I can include a sample invoice PDF layout when we meet.
